records.deidentified_narrative: police responded to the listed location, at 1157, for a major accident. caller called in and stated that a male had been struck by a tow truck at the location. upon arrival i contacted unit 4 who stated that unit 1 was called to the location by the owner of unit 2-3. unit 4 stated that unit 2 was going to be towed to a transmission shop to be serviced and unit 1 picked it up to take it there. unit 4 stated that as unit 1 was leaving, he was in between unit 2 and unit 3 looking at unit 3 and had the driver's door open. unit 4 stated that unit 1 began to take off and unit 2 struck the open door and he was pushed into the door as well. unit 4 stated that he began to yell at unit 1 driver to stop, but he did not hear or see him. unit 4 stated that he was almost crushed between unit 2 and unit 3's door. unit 4 stated that he does not believe that unit 1 driver knew that unit 2 had struck unit 3 and he left the location. ems arrived to the location to check on unit 4 but he refused treatment and stated that he was fine. i was able to speak to unit 1 driver, who was now at the secondary location, and he stated that he did not strike unit 3 while he was leaving and stated that now one tried to flag him down to advise him of the collision. unit 1 stated that he believes that unit 2-3 owner may have damaged unit 3 afterwards and is claiming that he caused the damage to file a claim on his insurance. bcso deputy j. arias made unit 1's location and confirmed that neither unit 1 nor unit 2 had any damage that indicated that they had struck unit 3. unit 3 had damage to the driver's door consistent with when a door is opened to far out. unit 1-2 owner's were given the [case id]. no further action was taken at this time. coban bwc

front of unit 1. unit 1 did not have time to react and unit 1 's left frontend struck unit 2. unit 2 was thrown airborne and landed approximately 30 ft north of the intersection in the roadway of esmeralda. upon arrival, unit 2 was unconscience but breathing. unit 2 sustained numerous cuts and abrasions to his face, arms, and legs. unit 2 had a large laceraction across the back of his head. unit 2 was following behind them. the witnesses stated that as they approached the intersection they turned southbound on esmeralda while unit 2 suddenly started running across esmeralda narrowly avoiding two vehicles travelling southbound. the witnesses stated the southbound vehicles honked at unit 2 and then unit 2 moved into unit 1'[roadway] of travel where unit 1 struck unit 2. the witnesses stated the driver of unit 2 screamed as she suddenly hit unit 2. the witnesses stated that unit 1 did not have enough time to react to avoid hitting unit 2. there was very faint nearly non visible crosswalk lines on the southside of the intersection crossing esmeralda but unit 2 was on the northside of the intersection. ems evaluated the driver of unit 1 where she admitted to using cocaine and smoking marijuana several hours prior to the incident. due to this voluntary statement, officer orta, j. #1079 made the location to evaluate the driver of unit 1 and determined her to show any current signs of impairment. both the driver and passenger of unit 1 stated they were not injured. sgt lueveno, m. #3343 and traffic investigation det. doyle, j. #2401 were notiied and made the locaiton. unit 2 was determined to have failed to yield right of way to unit 1. the driver of unit 1 was issued the listed citaiton for driving with an invalid license.

records.deidentified_narrative: police responded to the listed location for a major accident. i arrived on scene and observed ap1's listed vehicle up against the listed building with visible damage caused by the same listed vehicle. i walked over the driver side of the listed vehicle where ap1 was standing. i asked the group of people standing around who was driving. two people next to ap1 pointed at ap1 and then ap1 also stated me, i tried to clarify with ap1 and asked ap1 if he was driving, to which ap1 responded yes. i then asked ap1 what happened to which he stated he did not know. i tried to ask questions to figure out some possible reasons for ap1's crash and he kept saying i do know what happened. ap1 then pointed to the opposite side of the listed restaurant and stated he was over there and now he was over this side. ap1 did not seem to understand how he got to the side of the building he was on or how he crashed. it also appeared that ap1 did not speak english well and i had to ask the lady standing next to ap1 to help me translate. i asked ap1 for his drivers license and ap1 stated he did not have one and that he lost it. i was able to get ap1's name and date of birth with the help of the waitress standing next to ap1. while ap1 was speaking to the waitress and trying to provide me with his information i was able to smell the strong odor of intoxicants to coming from ap1's breath as he spoke. i then walked inside to speak with v1. v1 stated she was sitting in the both on the inside of the wall in which ap1 backed his truck into. v1 stated she had just gotten married three weeks ago and they were showing her sister some pictures. v1 stated she had slid from the back of the bench to the side potion when ap1 came through the wall and v1 was struck by the wall and debris that fell into the restaurant. as i was leaving from inside the restaurant i was approached by a customer who advised me that he witnessed ap1 back into the listed location this customer was w3. he further advised me that he saw ap1 inside the listed location at the bar. this same witness advised me that ap1 was also inside the listed location sleeping. i then spoke with my cover officer who spoke with the three different witnesses. officer m. bennett#0519 stated that ap1 was parked on the opposite side of the restaurant. ap1 then backed out of the parking lot and struck a pole that was also on the opposite side of the restaurant. officer bennett then advised me that ap1 was seen [roadway] prior to him jumping the curb and smashing into the side of the building. i asked officer bennett where was ap1 and he stated that he placed him into the back of his patrol car but that he was only detained. officer [roadway] ap1 in handcuffs and only sat him in the car to detain him for further investigation. i was advised by fire bc6 that the vehicle was safe to move away from the building. i asked my cover officer to make sure the vehicle was off. officer bennett did so and took the keys out of the ignition. i then also requested a spanish speaking to assist with the dwi evaluation of ap1. officer castillo. c#1029 made the scene to assist with the spanish translation to english. while i was waiting for officer castillo i was advised by one of the waitress that v2 was also injured during this crash and was inside. v2 stated she was inside the listed location working when she was hit by a table that fell when ap1 came through the wall in his pickup truck. officer castillo arrived on scene and assisted me with my evaluation of ap1. i then spoke to ap1 and advised him that i was going to perform some field sobriety test to evaluate tests to see [roadway]. ap1 stated that would be fine. i began buy giving ap1 instructions on how to stand prior to me performing the hgn test. after officer castillo explained what was going to happened i performed the hgn test. i observed distinct and sustained nystagmus at maximum deviation in both eyes. i also observed onset of nystagmus prior to 45 degrees in both eyes. i was not able to observe a lack of smooth pursuit or vertical nystagmus. i then gave ap1 instructions on how to stand for the one leg stand test. once the instructions were given to ap1 and explained via officer castillo ap1 began. ap1 used his right leg and showed 4 clues. ap1 put his foot down three times and swayed visibly during the test. i then turned ap1 to face the yellow parking lot line and explained the walk and turn test. once i was done explaining i had officer castillo translate to ap1 and ap1 stated he understood. ap1 walked incorrectly when he did not touch heal to toe and raised his arms for balance and ap1 also did not [roadway] down. ap1 turned incorrectly by spinning around instead of taking small controlled steps. ap1 walked back to the starting point and again did not touch heal to toe or count out loud. ap1 also lifted his arms for balance. once ap1 was done i asked if ap1 understood the instructions to which he stated yes he did. ap1 was asked why he didn't count out loud when he stated he understood the instructions. ap1 then asked to perform the test a second time. i stated this would be fine since it ap1 said he understood the instructions now. ap1 walked down the line and counted out loud while walking. ap1 did touch heal to toe but raised his arms for balance while walking down. ap1 also did not turn correctly and just turned around instead of taking a series of small steps. ap1 then walked back towards the starting point while counting out loud. ap1 did touch heal to toe again but again also raised his arms for balance. since ap1 was now done with the tests i asked ap1 if he had anything to drink while inside the restaurant. ap1 stated that while he was inside here he had maybe about three or four. i tried to clarify what ap1 meant and he stated three or four beers, budweiser or bud lights. i also asked ap1 if he had eaten while inside the restaurant which he stated yes and [roadway] home when he left. i asked ap1 if when he left to head home [roadway]. ap1 stated yes, 100%. ap1 further stated that he felt safe enough to have his wife in the car. ap1 records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was travelling west in the parking lot of walmart located at 9235 [roadway] east. unit 2, a pedestrian, was exiting the store walking east and pushing a shopping cart east through the parking lot. unit 1 was turning south and struck the shopping cart with unit 1's front end (fc). unit 2 fell to the ground due to the contact of unit 1 with the shopping cart. unit 1 has a contributing factor for driver inattention to pedestrian traffic in a parking lot. unit 2 has a contributing factor for being inattentive to vehicular traffic in a parking lot. the operator of unit 1 stated that she was attempting to turn to park her car when she made contact with the shopping cart that the pedestrian was pushing. the operator stated she asked the pedestrian if she needed an ambulance but the pedestrian declined. the passenger of unit 1 stated that as they were travelling through the parking lot, the pedestrian intentionally shoved the shopping cart into the vehicle and fell backwards without being struck by the vehicle. the pedestrian claimed that she left the store when unit 1 struck her shopping cart causing her to fall to the ground. the pedestrian advised unit 1 struck the shopping cart, and never struck her, unit 2. the pedestrian declined medical treatment when asked by the investigating officer. video surveillance of the parking lot was viewed, and the crash was unable to be viewed directly. the video does show the pedestrian not crossing the throughway using the crosswalk, and shows the pedestrian in the middle of the throughway standing up after the impact, and pushing her shopping cart to her vehicle. when being informed of what the video showed, the pedestrian attempted to change her story, saying the shopping cart fell on top of her, and caused her injuries, and that she had to be helped up by multiple people. the video does not indicate this. the investigating officer does not find the pedestrian to be a credible witness. supplement info: on friday, december 29, 2017, [person], the pedestrian in this crash, contacted me claiming there was a witness to this crash that was not included. [person] me with the name and contact phone number of the witness. i contacted the reported witness, thelma carter, via telephone call. i was unable to confirm [person] via phone call. [person] that she witnessed [roadway] in september, 2017, sometime between 1:30pm and 2:00p. m. [person] that the pedestrian was in the crosswalk the whole time, and that the vehicle struck the shopping cart and [person], causing her leg injuries. [person] advised that the operator of unit 1 had alcohol on her breath. [person] that she left the scene prior to law enforcement arrival due to her need for oxygen. [person] that prior to my contacting her, she had spoken with [person] 1 month prior, and to [person], a few weeks prior. [person] about where the crash occurred does not match the surveillance video. [person] about the car striking [person], does not match [person] statements of what occurred. the operator of unit 1 did not have an odor of alcohol on her breath and did not appear to be impaired. the time and date of the crash according to [person] also incorrect. i determined that [person] not a reliable witness to this crash. i also observed that a shopping cart (originally listed as unit 3), is unable to be listed as a separate unit according to the cr-100, and was corrected. i also changed all instances of ""basket"" to ""shopping cart"" for clarity. witness info:thelma carter281-318-9995

records.deidentified_narrative: unit 2 was inside unit 1 backing the vehicle into her driveway at 202 n san ignacio. she said she was unable to stop the vehicle, so she jumped out of the drivers' side door and the vehicle continued to reverse with the door open, causing the door to strike one of the metal post supporting the car port of the driveway. she was unsure if her vehicle had run over her or if she hurt herself while jumping out, and kept saying she couldn't remember, but had pain in both legs. she had moved to a chair and was seated when i arrived on scene, and her daughter said when she arrived unit two was standing, had parked the vehicle, and cleaned off her legs. there were plants scattered off the driveway to the left hand side and a small garden bed outlined with rocks and bricks that she said she may have fell into. there was also a broken glass aquarium inside the bed that she was unsure if she had fallen into. it seemed from her injuries and the parked vehicle that she had most likely hurt herself while jumping out of the vehicle and had not been run over. medic 15 arrived and she was able to transfer herself onto a stretcher [medical facility].

records.public_safe_text: unit 1 was previously involved in a single vehicle accident, reference sapd17189038. while unit 1 was wrecked out on the main lanes, unit 2 was outside unit 1 accessing the damage. unit 2 was next to unit 1 when unit 3 collided with unit 1 and unit 2. due to wet roads and rainy weather, unit 3's driver, d3, was unable to see unit 1 and unit 2 ahead of time on the roadway. the collision caused unit 1 to spin and severely injure unit 2. both unit 1 and unit 3 came to a complete stop in the main lanes of traffic and unit 2's resting point was north of unit 1. unit 1's passenger, dp1, remained inside the vehicle and was not injured. unit 3's driver [medical facility] by ems [medical facility] in critical condition. detective r. villarreal #2021 made the scene, took photographs, and processed the accident scene. tid l. herries #2488 made the accident scene for further investigation.
